slots.title: Authoritative EMD/EEMD Filtering References
slots.instruction: Identify the EMD/EEMD filtering references that are most authoritative for engineering vibration or transient signal records. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Supported Component Removal Practices
slots.instruction: Assess what the literature supports regarding removal of high-frequency IMFs, residual or trend terms, or selected modal components in EMD/EEMD filtering and reconstruction. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Known Limitations To Report
slots.instruction: Explain the known limitations that should be reported, including mode mixing, end effects, non-uniqueness, sensitivity to ensemble or noise parameters, and loss of physical interpretability. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Validation Checks For EEMD-Filtered Histories
slots.instruction: Identify validation checks that are recommended or defensible for EEMD-filtered engineering histories, including peak preservation, energy preservation, frequency content, drift or baseline checks, response spectra, visual review, and any other relevant diagnostics. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Description Without Overclaiming
slots.instruction: Explain how EEMD filtering should be described without overclaiming that retained modes are physically unique blast-wave components. Write in flowing paragraphs.

constraints: Prepare material for an English technical report.
Focus on claim support, limitations, and validation expectations for EEMD as an engineering filtering/reconstruction method, not on basic definitions of EMD or EEMD.
